strategy_title: Autotune num_stages to Enable Async Prefetch in Triton
strategy_description: When a Triton kernel shows >70% no-eligible-warp cycles and a dominant L1TEX scoreboard stall (>50% of CPI), the hardware cannot hide memory latency with the available active warps. Adding @triton.autotune with configs that sweep num_stages (2–4) alongside XBLOCK/YBLOCK/num_warps enables the Triton compiler to emit async prefetch instructions, overlapping the next tile's data fetch with current-tile compute. In this case, warp cycles per issued instruction dropped from 54.2 to 29.2 and eligible warps per scheduler rose from 0.57 to 1.0, yielding a 1.19x speedup (66.2 µs → 55.7 µs); the trade-off is higher register pressure (32→40 registers/thread) which reduced theoretical occupancy from 100% to 75%.
applicable_when: Triton pointwise/elementwise kernel with: (1) no-eligible-warp cycles >60%, (2) dominant L1TEX scoreboard stall >40% of CPI, (3) L1 hit rate <10%, (4) current num_stages=1 (single-stage pipeline), (5) kernel body is simple (few loads, one FMA, one store) making it amenable to Triton's pipeline lowering.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel is already register-bound (registers/thread near hardware max); increasing num_stages raises register pressure and may reduce occupancy enough to hurt performance. Also avoid when the kernel has complex control flow or data-dependent branches that prevent static prefetch scheduling. Not applicable when the bottleneck is compute-bound (SM throughput >80%) rather than memory-latency-bound.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: num_stages in triton.Config controls the software pipeline depth emitted by the Triton compiler (async prefetch). Equivalent concept in CUDA is __pipeline_memcpy_async / cp.async with pipeline stages. The grid must be changed from a static tuple to a lambda meta: (...) so autotune can inject the selected XBLOCK/YBLOCK. The kernel call site must drop explicit XBLOCK/YBLOCK kwargs.
